title: East County Library / Holst Architecture
text:
East County Library / Holst Architecture

Today, Holst Architecture released the official photography for the new East County Library, a community-focused destination for learning, play, and connection in Gresham, Oregon. A critical civic space missing in the area for decades, the library's innovative programming and thoughtful architecture were shaped to serve the current and future needs of over 100,000 residents.

title: Grande Nef de l'Île-des-Vannes Renovation / Chatillon Architectes
text:
Grande Nef de l'Île-des-Vannes Renovation / Chatillon Architectes

Following seven years of closure, Chatillon Architectes implements contemporary solutions and state-of-the-art facilities, bringing this distinctive building back to life, first as an Olympic training site and then for its subsequent return to the local community. The first images of the restored Grande Nef de l'Île-des-Vannes sports complex in Paris have been revealed ahead of its role as an Olympic training facility. Featuring a sweeping parabolic roof and striking translucent side paneling, the unique structure was designed by Anatole Kopp, Lucien Metrich, and Pierre Chazanoff in 1971, and closed in 2018 due to decay and accessibility issues. Adapting the building for contemporary use, Chatillon Architectes has fully restored the structure, installing contemporary energy solutions, structural repairs, universal accessibility upgrades and state-of-the-art facilities, from acoustic paneling to sports flooring to lighting fixtures.

title: Imaging Heaven
text:
Imaging Heaven

Imaging Heaven is a visual narrative of frescoed church ceilings, photographed across Italy and Catholic Europe. Moving from the Proto-Renaissance to the Baroque, the book follows painters as they confront a fundamental problem: how to make the unseen realm of heaven perceptible amid profound shifts in cosmology, theology, and science.

Guided by threads of light, gesture, and illusion, the photographs reveal how painters moved from shadowless gold grounds rooted in Byzantine techniques to radiant, sophisticated illumination; turned hieratic icons into anatomically precise, emotionally charged bodies; and dissolved architectural boundaries with a photographic study of trompe-l’oeil, quadratura, and di sotto in sù

title: ICA Miami Appoints Gensler to Design Second Museum Building in Miami Design District
text:
ICA Miami Appoints Gensler to Design Second Museum Building in Miami Design District

The Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami (ICA Miami) has appointed Gensler to lead the renovation and expansion of its second building in Miami's Design District, with the project scheduled to open in late 2027. Acquired by the museum in 2024, the building is located on the same block as its existing facility and will add 30,000 square feet of space, doubling ICA Miami's facilities. The expansion will introduce new galleries, educational spaces, and venues for public programming, establishing a multi-site campus intended to extend the museum's exhibition and community activities.

title: "Earth Craft" at the U.S. Pavilion Will Trace the Work of Builders at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
text:
"Earth Craft" at the U.S. Pavilion Will Trace the Work of Builders at the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale

The United States' contribution to the 20th International Architecture Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia will explore the relationship between the country's architecture, landscapes, and the people who shape it. Titled Earth Craft, the exhibition will be commissioned, organized, and curated by a team from the University of Miami School of Architecture (U-SoA). The lead curator, Professor Germane Barnes, conceived the exhibition as a representation of the United States "through its makers and not through its icons," recognizing that celebrated buildings were raised by anonymous builders who dug, shaped, and fired architectural legacy. Vyta Pivo, assistant professor, curator, and historian of Earth Craft, adds a contemporary approach by translating inherited knowledge of soil, water, and heat into computational design, conceiving craftwork and robotic fabrication as complementary. The exhibition will occupy the United States Pavilion at the Giardini della Biennale between May 8 and November 21, 2027, tracing earthen materials from the ground to finished buildings.

title: What materials meet the demands of a contemporary kitchen?
text:
What materials meet the demands of a contemporary kitchen?

The contemporary kitchen is no longer just a space for food preparation; it has become one of the most dynamic areas of the home. Design decisions can redefine both spatial configurations and the layout of elements as they integrate with various social areas, incorporate new technologies, or adapt to changing domestic habits. In this scenario, and in response to multiple needs, the balance between functionality, comfort, durability, and aesthetics is directly linked to the selection of finishing materials. Depending on the countertop finish or the cabinet opening system, each kitchen configuration helps build environments tailored to different activities and ways of living.

title: Master Plan Meets Land: Planning Amaravati, India’s New State Capital
text:
Master Plan Meets Land: Planning Amaravati, India’s New State Capital

A new capital is usually introduced through its principal buildings: the assembly, the secretariat and the ceremonial spaces that give a seat of government its public image. In Amaravati, India's Andhra Pradesh, that image of a new capital sits within an older landscape of cultivated fields, villages and established routes. Before the capital project, the region was already occupied by agricultural villages, local roads and settlements connected to the Krishna River and its water systems. The capital project is reorganizing this agrarian territory into a planned administrative city, bringing existing settlements and land ownership into the process of urban development. Its architectural identity will depend on how the new buildings, infrastructure, and public spaces relate to the settlements and landscapes already there.

text:
The Giant's Garden Daycare / design CHOU

The Giant's Garden is a children's activity space inspired by Oscar Wilde's fairy tale The Selfish Giant. In the story, winter lingers in the garden while children are kept out, and spring returns when they come back. The project began with the idea of creating a garden within the city, brought to life by children's activities. Here, children explore soil and shape dough, while parents take a moment away from their daily routines and rest nearby.

title: Populus / Studio Gang
text:
Populus / Studio Gang

Studio Gang, the international architecture and urban design firm led by Jeanne Gang, has completed Populus, a 265-room hotel poised to become a new social center for downtown Denver. Marking Studio Gang's first completed project in Colorado and the American Southwest region, Populus's design draws from the growth processes of the state's native Aspen trees (Populus tremuloides) to establish a new architectural icon for Denver. "Denver strikes a unique balance between being a vibrant city and a gateway to some of the country's most awe-inspiring natural landscapes. Our goal was to draw from this distinct urban character and rich ecology to create a building that would help define the skyline of this thriving city," says Jeanne Gang, Founding Partner of Studio Gang.
